Plot how well a context tree predicts new sequences

Source: R/plot_diagnostics.R
plot_predictive.Rd

plot_predictive() plots how much probability a context tree gives to what happens next in sequences it has not seen, the measure of its value as a predictive model. It scores every transition of held-out sequences with score_positions() and shows where the model is confident and where it is surprised.

type = "position" plots the probability given to each observed next state against its position in the sequence. type = "ecdf" plots the empirical cumulative distribution of those probabilities, showing how often the model gives high or low probability to what actually happened. type = "logloss" plots the per-transition log-loss \(-\log_2 P(\mathrm{observed})\) in bits against position, with the mean at each position and the overall mean; 0 bits is a certain and correct prediction.

For one number summarizing held-out prediction use perplexity(), and to choose the settings that minimize it use tune_tree().

Usage

plot_predictive(tree, newdata, type = c("position", "ecdf", "logloss"))

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object.

newdata

Held-out sequences in any format accepted by context_tree().

type

"position" (default), "ecdf" or "logloss".

Value

A ggplot object of the scored transitions.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input

(error) tree is not a transitiontrees object.

transitiontrees_empty_result

(error) newdata has no transitions to score.

See also

score_positions() for the scored transitions as a table; perplexity(); tune_tree().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 2)
held_out <- head(engagement, 40)
plot_predictive(tree, held_out)

plot_predictive(tree, held_out, type = "ecdf")

plot_predictive(tree, held_out, type = "logloss")
